correctness.rationale: At common N and P with strictly positive confusion cells, exhaustive allowed TP∈[1,P−1], FP∈[1,N−P−1], FN=P−TP, TN=N−P−FP is complete. The exact rational identities B=(TP/P+TN/(N−P))/2, G²=TP·TN/[P(N−P)] and G²=B²−(s−c)²/4 hold. B>1/2 iff TP·TN>FP·FN. Fresh independently written exact Fraction census gives eligible-table/pair/weak/strict counts for N=4..11: (0,0,0,0),(2,0,0,0),(3,0,0,0),(10,8,0,0),(15,17,2,0),(26,48,4,0),(38,93,6,0),(60,216,16,6). Thus first weak disagreement N=8 and first strict reversal N=11, exactly six unordered pairs modulo three class-label flips. Explicit N=11 P=3 pairs (1,1,2,7) and (2,4,1,4) give B 29/48>7/12 but G² 7/24<1/3.

value.rationale: Balanced accuracy and the sensitivity–specificity geometric mean are canonical scores for imbalanced classification; a complete smallest-test-set boundary after realistic same-prevalence and nondegenerate above-chance restrictions is a motivated exact decision comparability threshold. Six first-layer reversals distinguish genuine opposite strict choices from mere ties. It does not claim statistical superiority of either score.
